title: Crime
subtitle: burglary, evidence, trial, sentence
summary: Name crimes and the people who commit them, and follow a case through arrest, investigation, trial, verdict and sentence.

lesson.heading: Crimes and criminals
rows: taking something illegally into another country
taking a person hostage in exchange for money or other favours
deceiving people in order to take money from them
taking someone, especially a child, usually in order to harm them
lesson.note: All these verbs are regular. Terrorise is mainly used generally, meaning to make others very frightened, rather than just for the crime.

lesson.heading: Investigating crime
lesson.text: Ross **committed a crime** when he **robbed** a bank. Someone **witnessed** the crime and told the police. The police **arrested** Ross and **charged him with** bank robbery. They also **accused** his twin brother Ben **of** being his **accomplice**.

examples.text: The police **investigated the case** and collected **evidence** at the **crime scene**.
examples.note: evidence = information used in court to decide whether the accused is guilty; a case = a crime that is being investigated

examples.text: They found Ross's **fingerprints** and **DNA evidence** that linked him to the crime.
examples.note: DNA evidence comes from hair or skin and can be shown scientifically to come from a particular person

examples.text: They were confident they had **proof** that the two men were **guilty**.
examples.note: proof = evidence that shows conclusively whether something is a fact

lesson.heading: The trial
lesson.text: The case **came to court** and the two men were **tried**. The **trial** did not last long. Both **pleaded not guilty**. Their lawyer did her best to **defend** them, but the **prosecuting lawyer** produced a very strong case against them.

examples.text: After brief deliberations, the **jury passed verdict** on them.
Ross was **convicted of** robbery, but Ben was **innocent**.
examples.note: be convicted of = be found guilty of a crime

examples.text: The judge **acquitted** Ben of any involvement in the robbery.

lesson.heading: Punishment
lesson.text: The judge **sentenced** Ross **to** three years in **prison**. As well as a **prison sentence**, he also had to pay a large **fine**.

examples.text: Ross **served** two years in prison, but was **released from prison** a year early.
He got **time off** for good behaviour.

lesson.heading: People in the legal process
rows: someone who commits an illegal act (an **offence**)
the person who leads a trial and decides on the **sentence**, i.e. the punishment
a group of citizens (12 in the UK) who decide on the **verdict**, i.e. whether the accused is guilty
a person who suffers as the result of a crime
a person who is suspected of committing an offence
a person who sees a crime being committed

lesson.text: Watch the prepositions: charge someone with a crime, accuse someone of a crime, suspect someone of a crime, convict someone of a crime, but sentence someone to a punishment.

exercises.prompt: Which crime is each person accused of?

pairs.left: Zoe stole a chocolate bar from a shop.
Harry took a film star's son and demanded a large sum of money.
Ophelia shot her husband in the heart.
Noah tried to take cigarettes into his country without paying tax.
Tom broke into someone's house and stole a TV.
Mike sold people holiday homes that didn't really exist.

exercises.prompt: Match each person with the description.

pairs.right: leads the trial and decides on the sentence
decides whether the accused is guilty
suffers as the result of a crime
is thought to have committed an offence

exercises.prompt: A man has been ___ by police after a house in the city centre was broken into last night.
exercises.explanation: The police arrest someone before charging them.

exercises.prompt: The man has been charged ___ burglary.
exercises.explanation: You charge someone with a crime.

exercises.prompt: Experts have searched the crime ___ and taken several items away.
exercises.explanation: Police collect evidence at the crime scene.

exercises.prompt: The items will be used as ___ in court.
exercises.explanation: Evidence is the information used in court to decide guilt.

exercises.prompt: The police believe the burglar may have had an ___, so they are looking for a second man.
exercises.explanation: An accomplice helps someone commit a crime.

exercises.prompt: They are calling for anyone who ___ the crime to come forward.
exercises.explanation: To witness a crime is to see it being committed.

exercises.prompt: Many prisoners end up getting time ___ for good behaviour.
exercises.explanation: Time off means part of the sentence is not served.

exercises.prompt: The two girls are suspected ___ taking sweets from the shop without paying.
exercises.explanation: You suspect someone of doing something.

exercises.prompt: The jury passed a verdict of guilty ___ the accused.
exercises.explanation: A jury passes verdict on someone.

exercises.prompt: The judge ___ the accused to six months in prison.
The police think Bert is guilty but they have no ___.
exercises.explanation: Proof shows conclusively that something is a fact.

exercises.prompt: In court the accused ___ not guilty.
exercises.explanation: To plead not guilty is to say in court that you did not commit the crime.

exercises.prompt: The murder case is still under ___ by the police.
exercises.explanation: A case that is being looked into is under investigation.

exercises.prompt: The bank robbers are currently on ___ at a court in London.
exercises.explanation: Someone being tried in court is on trial.

exercises.statement: Nathan is hoping to be released from prison soon.
exercises.explanation: Correct - you are released from prison when you are let out.
